instructionText: Lead with the answer, then explain.
Start sentences with the actor doing the thing, then the verb.
Prefer plain Anglo-Saxon words to Latinate ones: "use" over "utilize", "start" over "initiate", "so" over "consequently", "because" over "insofar as".
Cut every phrase that does not change the meaning if removed.
source: run 2 — 6 tasks x 5 replicates, n=30. See LIB_RPT_qualifier-carveout_2026-08-02.md
rescoredAt: 0.3.0 — the HEDGE_IGNORE_DEFAULT and CLARITY_IGNORE_DEFAULT fixes changed directness and clarity scores, moving the composite from 83.6 to 89.4 and clarity from 54.1 to 90.7. No gated metric is affected: words, jargonPct, sentenceSimplicity and gradeBand are independent dimensions and are unchanged.

versionDrift.note: The means below were taken on 0.3.0. `compare.mjs` prints the scoring version and flags a difference without failing on one — see its comment for why.
versionDrift.checked: 0.4.2, 2026-08-08. Re-scored run 2's E arm (eval/out-run2, n=30) at HEAD: words 290.1, jargonPct 8.7, sentenceSimplicity 69.2, gradeBand 98.5 — every gated metric identical to the recorded means. The ungated composite moved 89.4 -> 90.2, from the 0.4.x directness changes.
versionDrift.implication: Gated metrics have been stable across five releases because they live in `readability` and in `stats`, and every release since has changed `style`. Do not read that as a guarantee: re-run this check when a release touches readability or the parser, and record the result here.

tolerances.note: Judgment calls, not derived from a variance estimate. They are set to catch a register change, not to detect small drifts. Widen them rather than chase noise.

words.rationale: Baseline 290.1 against a within-run control of 437.9. 360 sits between them, nearer the baseline, so drifting most of the way back to uninstructed length trips it.

jargonPct.rationale: Baseline 8.7 against a within-run control of 10.7. 10.5 trips just before vocabulary returns to uninstructed levels.

sentenceSimplicity.rationale: Sits between E's observed range (69.2 run 2, 69.9 run 3) and E', which scored 60.3 and was called a style regression. The within-run control scored 50.2, so this also catches a full reversion. A judgment call — the gate should agree with the report.

gradeBand.rationale: Catches over-simplification. Variant C hit 57.6 by falling below the band floor.

reproduced: run 3 (2026-08-03, same model) independently reproduced E on the same task set: words 297.8, jargonPct 8.7, sentenceSimplicity 69.9, gradeBand 99.3. Every gated metric within 3% of the recorded means, so the means below are left at run 2 and the tolerances are calibrated against them.

control.description: No style instruction at all, same six tasks, 5 replicates, n=30. Measured in run 3 so the comparison is within-run rather than across task sets.
control.deltaFromControl: E cuts length 32% (437.9 -> 297.8), cuts jargon 2.0 points (10.7 -> 8.7), and raises sentence-simplicity 19.7 points (50.2 -> 69.9). These supersede the earlier cross-task-set figures, which compared against a 4-task control of 550 words and so overstated the length effect as ~40%.

modelTransfer.tested: claude-sonnet-5, 2026-08-03, same ten tasks — see LIB_RPT_multi-model_2026-08-03.md
modelTransfer.finding: Ranking transfers, magnitude does not. Sonnet's uninstructed output is already 258.6 words against Opus's 475.3, so there is far less headroom: E moves it -12% on length against -41% on Opus, and +6.8 sentence-simplicity against +17.0.
modelTransfer.deploymentNote: The character budget is tier-dependent. On Sonnet the 176-char compression is indistinguishable from the full 315-char rules (230.4 vs 226.5 words, 10.5 vs 10.2 jargon); on Opus the full form buys 16 points of length reduction. Haiku untested.
